page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A1.Flex.16-32 is a compute-oriented virtual machine instance built on the 64-bit Arm architecture. The configuration provides 16 dedicated physical cores powered by the Ampere Altra processor operating at a sustained clock speed of 3.0 GHz. Because each core runs a single hardware thread, the instance provides 16 dedicated vCPUs without the performance variability associated with simultaneous multithreading. System memory is configured at 32.0 GB, yielding a memory allocation of 2.0 GB per physical core.

The hardware configuration does not bundle local disk storage, requiring persistence to be provisioned via attached network block volumes. It contains zero GPU accelerators, focusing purely on general and compute-bound central processing. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Across cloud infrastructure deployments, the Ampere Altra platform offers high core density and linear multi-threaded scaling, delivering efficient throughput per vCPU for code compiled to arm64 instruction sets.

With its 1:2 memory-to-core ratio and dedicated core pipeline, this instance is suitable for compute-centric workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. Common deployment profiles include software build and CI/CD pipelines targeting Arm architectures, web application clusters, containerized microservices, video encoding, and batch data processing.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A1.Flex.16-32 is an Arm-based virtual machine configured with 16 dedicated physical cores from the Ampere Altra processor family running at 3.0 GHz. Each vCPU maps directly to a physical core with one thread per core, eliminating hyperthreading interference and ensuring predictable execution across all 16 execution threads. The instance provides 32.0 GB of system memory, matching a 2.0 GB per core ratio suited for compute-focused applications. There is no bundled local storage included in the hardware profile, meaning block storage must be attached over the network, and the profile includes no GPU acceleration. One complimentary public IPv4 address is provided. VM.Standard.A1.Flex.16-32 is well aligned for Arm-native development, automated CI/CD build environments, media transcoding, containerized microservices, and web serving workloads.
